title: Compact policy sync gap causes transient duplicate allow
creator: Priya Shah
description: Intermittent customer reports and internal dashboards show short windows where requests against the same route/key are permitted twice (duplicate allowance) immediately after policy compaction and leader handoff. The behavior appears as a brief unmetered spike for affected orgs and routes and leads to undercounted usage and transient SLA violations for metering accuracy.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy policy rewrite that triggers compaction (e.g., hierarchical policy consolidation) on a multi-shard test cluster
2) Simulate steady traffic to a single org/route/key (200 rps) while forcing leader handoff of the policy shard (kill leader pod)
3) Observe per-key enforcer logs and meter increments during the handoff window
4) Query time-series metering dashboard for the route and inspect raw event ingestion for duplicate allows
observed_behavior: During leader handoff that coincides with a policy compaction job, the enforcer occasionally emits an 'ALLOW' decision twice for the same logical token window. The first allow increments the meter; the second allow is not accompanied by the expected debit (or in some paths the debit occurs but is dropped before aggregation), producing a transient undercount. This manifests as a 30-120s plateau in per-key token usage where requests succeed but the accumulated usage jumps later after reconciliation.
expected_behavior: Policy compaction and leader transitions should not create windows where duplicate ALLOW decisions bypass debit accounting. Enforcer should serialize compaction application and leader handoff such that the authoritative debit emitter is unique and idempotent for each request.
root_cause: Race between compaction-applier and the shard leader selection: compaction replaces route-derived policy objects and briefly disables the per-request debit stamp. During leader handoff the new leader's compaction-applier believes certain cached 'allow stamps' are authoritative and re-emits ALLOW decisions for requests that were already allowed by the old leader. In some code paths the debit emitter runs on the old leader but the acknowledgment path to the aggregator is interrupted during handoff, causing a mismatch between allow events and debit records.
mitigation:
1) Rollout a short-term guard: block compaction application during in-flight leader handoff by delaying compaction commits when a leader election is detected (feature flag gated).
2) Backfill affected windows: run a reconciliation job to scan ingestion logs and re-insert missing debits for detected duplicate-allow windows for impacted orgs.
3) Notify customers with potential exposure and open billing tickets for validated misses.
long_term_fix: Redesign policy compaction to use a two-phase commit with an explicit stamping version that both leaders and followers check before emitting ALLOW decisions. Introduce idempotent debit tokens (monotonic request IDs + per-shard sequence) persisted to a small durable store so duplicate ALLOWs cannot produce unmetered success. Also add a per-request acknowledgment handshake between enforcer and aggregator to guarantee eventual debit reconciliation.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (hotfix): enable feature-flag that prevents compaction during leader election across all clusters (canary on internal clusters first) — estimated 2 hours to roll out
Phase 2 (reconciliation): run backfill job for last 48 hours of ingestion for affected shards, validate against request logs and issue customer credits where necessary — estimated 1 day
Phase 3 (tech debt): implement idempotent debit tokens and two-phase compaction commit, land in runtime-1.24 and Dedicated agents — estimated 3 sprints
Phase 4: gradual rollout with expanded tracing and a reconciliation alert — add automated post-handoff audits
